Prediction grid at a chosen resolution

Source: R/grid.R
bruce_grid.Rd

Builds a raster covering a polygon at the requested cell size, with cells outside the polygon set to NA (cell centre inside the polygon), ready for the grid argument of bruce_predict(), bruce_decompose() and bruce_zonal().

Usage

bruce_grid(domain, resolution, crs = NULL)

Arguments

domain

Polygon(s) (sf, sfc or SpatVector).

resolution

Cell size in the units of the projection (metres).

crs

Projection of the grid: anything sf::st_crs() accepts, or a bruce_data / bruce_fit to use the model's projection. NULL keeps the domain's projection, which must then be projected.

Value

A single-layer terra::SpatRaster named grid, 1 inside the domain and NA outside.

Details

The grid resolution sets where the surface is evaluated, not how much spatial detail the model has. The spatial field varies on the scale of the mesh and of the station network (kilometres), so a finer grid adds detail only through the covariates. Two consequences:

  • covariates need native data at least as fine as the grid, or the map shows the blocks of the coarser raster;

  • a coefficient refers to the covariate as it was measured at the stations. If urban fraction was the mean over a 500 m block, predicting at 100 m with urban fraction averaged over 100 m cells gives larger contrasts than the model learned. Keep the covariate's support (e.g. a 500 m moving-window mean computed at 100 m) when refining the grid.

Prediction time and memory grow with the number of cells: halving the cell size multiplies them by four, and posterior samples kept with keep_samples = TRUE take cells x samples x days x 8 bytes.

Examples

sim <- bruce_simulate(n_days = 2, seed = 1)
g <- bruce_grid(sim$domain, resolution = 1000)
g
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 30, 30, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 650000, 680000, 7450000, 7480000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : SIRGAS 2000 / UTM zone 23S (EPSG:31983)
#> source(s)   : memory
#> name        : grid
#> min value   :    1
#> max value   :    1
